lines.vo: Why do you grab your phone the second you get bored?
That's not just a phone problem. Your brain really hates doing nothing.
Kev writes down every bored grab in his Break the Habit tracker.
In one study, people sat alone with their thoughts for up to 15 minutes, next to a button that gave a mild shock.
About two thirds of the men, and a quarter of the women, shocked themselves at least once.
Just sitting with your thoughts can feel weirdly hard, so your brain grabs anything.
So next time you're bored, wait one minute before you reach for the phone.
One bored minute, one check mark. That's how you stay on track.

hook: People chose a *shock* over being bored
